A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main sections and Appendices A–E. Text, equations, figures and tables can be matched reliably despite bibliography reformatting and changed pagination.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D report original image-density estimation, synthetic Spinner/Spiral density fits, optimizer comparisons, and GPU time and memory measurements.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D retain the original image and synthetic density-estimation experiments, optimizer comparisons, and computational benchmarks.

M1.justification: The orthogonality and unitarity conditions, marginalization procedures, circuit constructions, and LandingPC optimizer adaptation remain unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Appendices A and E.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST, FashionMNIST, synthetic Spinner and Spiral data, and the same computational benchmarking scenarios. Section 6 adds reasons for choosing image benchmarks without expanding the evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same conventional and unitary squared PCs, product-layer configurations, and SGD, Adam, LandingSGD and LandingPC comparisons. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix D retains the same validation split, pixel encoding, model-size sweeps, optimizer hyperparameters, synthetic-data training settings and benchmarking procedure. The expanded experimental motivation does not revise these settings.

E4.justification: Appendix D retains the Fourier-versus-Gaussian comparisons, Hadamard-versus-Kronecker analyses, optimizer modifications study and numerical normalization checks. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables D.1–D.2 retain means and standard deviations across three random initializations, and Figure D.2 retains its three-initialization reporting. Appendix D.3 still averages measurements over 50 iterations after 10 burn-in iterations.

E6.justification: Figure 5, Figures D.1–D.2 and Tables D.1–D.3 retain the same results and entries. For example, Table D.1 reports 1.1923 ± 0.0007 MNIST bpd for the 16-unit Kronecker unitary model in both versions.

T1.justification: The definitions, Theorems 1–3, Appendix A assumptions and proofs, Appendix B tensor-network derivations, and Appendix E optimizer equations are unchanged. Citation-label revisions do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient marginalization, support for broader circuit factorizations, and more efficient learning with retained empirical performance. The revised evaluation framing does not change these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6 explicitly states that evaluation targets comparisons between unitary and conventional squared PCs rather than state-of-the-art performance. It also explains image-benchmark selection through community practice and the optimization challenges enabled by high-dimensional data. These are limited additions to the evaluation's rationale and scope.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement changes from supplying code as supplementary material to providing a direct repository link for implementations, experiment/result scripts and environment instructions. Appendix D's implementation details, hardware and hyperparameters remain unchanged; the change concerns documented code access.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Liu et al. (2023) and Garg et al. (2025) to motivate image benchmarks. Appendix C adds Zellinger et al. (2026) on expectation estimation using squared PCs. Most other citation changes concern metadata or formatting of already cited works.

P1.justification: Section 6 receives localized rewrites and expanded motivation, and the reproducibility statement is revised. Bibliographic entries are shortened and reformatted, with citation metadata edits throughout. The main narrative structure and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 5's caption is expanded to explain avoiding explicit circuit squaring when computing the partition function. An ICLR 2026 running header and text/reference reflow change the layout. No figures or tables are added or removed, and their diagrams, plotted data and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves clarity and usability by making the experimental purpose and benchmark rationale explicit, providing a direct code-repository pointer, and adding relevant research context. These are limited gains in framing and documented reproducibility access; the methods, proofs and empirical support remain unchanged.
